text:
maya: Heads up: found a funky mismatch in the sample-rerank flow. When using the JS batching helper + rust-sdk client we get a shape mismatch: server returns 1024-d vectors but our reranker expects 1536. Python sampleapp still gets 1536. Seems environment-dependent.

julian: oy. are these coming from the same model id? which endpoint: /embeddings or /rerank/embeddings?

maya: /embeddings. Model is open-embed-1536-v2. Request from rust client (conceptual):
```json
{
  "items": ["t1","t2"],
  "client_meta": {"app":"sample-rerank"}
}
```

maya: Response we observed in node path:
```json
{ "embeddings": [[0.01,...] /* len=1024 */ , [0.02,...] /* len=1024 */ ], "model":"open-embed-1536-v2" }
```

maya: Python path: same model, same inputs -> returns 1536 vectors as expected.

sam: interesting. Could be quantization/fastpath: the runtime picks a quantized kernel on certain hosts producing 1024-length by aggressive projection? Not expected. Any logs?

anya: also saw field swap in a couple of traces where response field was named "embedding" singular instead of "embeddings" array. That would totally break the rerank map.

julian: field renames + shape changes smell like a handler mix: maybe /embeddings v2 vs v1. ops-bot can you pull routing trace for the request id?

ops-bot: routing trace: recv->batcher->embed-fastpath-hostA(v1)->fallback->embed-compat-hostB(v2)

maya: exact trace:
[2026-04-01T09:13:00Z] recv POST /embeddings items=2 client=sample-rerank
[2026-04-01T09:13:00Z] enqueue Batcher shard=7 id=sh-221
[2026-04-01T09:13:01Z] dispatch to embed-fastpath-hostA handler=embed-handler-v2 quant=fp16 proj=1024
[2026-04-01T09:13:01Z] fallback to embed-compat-hostB handler=embed-handler-v1 proj=1536 field=embeddings

maya: note the projection param in logs. hostA advertises proj=1024. Why would it advertise 1024 for model that should be 1536?

sam: that indicates model variant mismatch in model catalog. Maybe hostA has an older quantized build of open-embed that projects to 1024 to save memory. Shouldn't happen for model pinned by customer. Are you using a pinned model version?

maya: sampleapp used model alias "open-embed-1536" not pinned. Good call. When retry happens the routing can pick a different host with different artifacts. Also, the batching helper compresses combined requests and sometimes rewrites fields when sending to fastpath to reduce bandwidth (field "embeddings" -> "embedding_vector_list") - I found that in the helper code.

julian: solution sprawl: (1) we must treat output vector dimension as part of model contract and fail fast if mismatch, (2) gateway should normalize field names and add compatibility shim, (3) batching helper should avoid rewriting field names or at least map them back on response, (4) sampleapps should pin model version for deterministic dims.

maya: short repro attached: small curl that toggles a header to force fastpath vs compat. repro gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/embed-dim-parity-probe

sam: let's also add an internal integration test that exercises: token expiry + retry + batch merge + fastpath/compat split, assert response.count == input_count and vector_length == model_expected_dim. Put it under devex/integration/embeddings/parity.

anya: for SDK parity: rust-sdk was using batching helper separately from node/python. We should centralize batching helper behavior in SDK-common lib so all languages honor idempotency keys and field mappings.

julian: agreed. I'll open RUNTIME-embed-223 to pin model artifact selection logic during a single request and to expose model_dim in capability handshake so gateway/batcher can verify.

maya: bandaid: sample-rerank updated to verify vector length before applying rerank; if mismatch, log and retry with explicit model_version param. Also changed client to set per-item idempotency keys so retries don't duplicate entries.

ops-bot: deploy notice: batching-helper@1.3.5 -> 1.3.6 (honor idempotency_key + avoid field renames) deploying to dev cluster.

julian: followups: 1) docs: clarify "embeddings" field and vector dim expectations in API spec; 2) SDKs: add parity tests for rust/node/python around batch retry; 3) infra: block routing downgrade for merged batches and surface model_dim in routing decisions.

maya: tl;dr: root cause = model alias + mixed handler versions + batching helper field rewrite + retry/re-enqueue. Fixes in flight: batching helper change, gateway shim, infra pin ticket, SDK parity tests. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

sam: nice triage. If anyone sees "embedding" vs "embeddings" or dims != expected, ping #devex and include request id.

maya: adding note to the sampleapp README so new onboarders pin model_version by default to avoid silent dim surprises.
